hypothesis: A curvature effect in a numerical Jacobi field is meaningful only where it exceeds the integrator error; the working expectation was that weak curvature (small |K| L^3/6) is the hard case for coarse steps and low-order methods.
input_data: 14 declared paths of length 2.0: plane, cylinder, sphere R=1, sphere R=10, sphere R=100, sphere R=1e4, sphere R=1e7, sphere R=1e8, torus R=2, torus R=64 equator, saddle c=1, bump h=0.5, bump h=0.05, hyperbolic k=1
Plane and cylinder with K recomputed from their second fundamental form
References: cancellation-free closed forms for constant curvature, DP45 at rtol 1e-12 (checked at 1e-11) otherwise

Error decomposition: exact rational step matrices for constant K; for variable K the observed error with a rounding estimate from a rerun with the heading column scaled by 3; an entry is rounding-affected when its rounding part exceeds 0.1 of its truncation part (declared)
mathematical_model: Signal S = |j_head(L) - L| (zero on flat surfaces; |K| L^3/6 for small constant K). Truncation error E(h) ~ C h^p. For j'' + K j = 0 the Euler and midpoint errors are themselves proportional to K (the K-free part j = s is integrated exactly), so S/E is independent of K as K -> 0; the RK4 error enters at O(K^2 h^4), so S/E grows like 1/K. For constant K the Jacobi part of every explicit Runge-Kutta stage is linear, so a run's deviation is the method's step matrix to the power N plus rounding; evaluating that matrix in exact rational arithmetic separates the truncation part from the rounding part exactly. The limit is floating point: when S approaches ulp(L) = 4.4e-16 the computed deviation is rounded away. Resolved when S/E >= 10 for every finer step.
numerical_result: Min RK4 ratio over truncation-dominated entries with N >= 16: 1.174e+05 (hyperbolic k=1, N = 16); the weakest signal with truncation-dominated RK4 errors (sphere R=100, S = 0.000133) is resolved from N = 4; RK4 errors are rounding-affected at every N >= 16 for sphere R=1e4, sphere R=1e7, sphere R=1e8. At N = 16, ratio(K = 1e-2)/ratio(K = 1): Euler 0.639, midpoint 0.412 (weaker is harder there); ratio(K = 1e-8)/ratio(K = 1e-2): Euler 0.9964, midpoint 0.9838; RK4 ratio gain from K = 1e-2 to 1e-4: 98; K = 1e-16: computed deviation 0 for all runs (max ratio 1) while the exact-arithmetic truncation errors alone give ratios of at least 42.9 at N = 128; K = 1e-14 (signal 30 ulp(L)): the Euler and midpoint errors at N = 4 are 0.987 and 1.08 times their exact-arithmetic truncation errors, so they are truncation errors, while every RK4 error is rounding (exact-arithmetic truncation at most 9e-31); orders euler 1.04, midpoint 1.9, rk4 3.89; flat max |j - L| 0 with second-form max |K| 0. Resolved from N by the truncation part alone: euler: N = 32 (sphere R=1, sphere R=10, sphere R=100, sphere R=1e4, sphere R=1e7, sphere R=1e8, torus R=2, torus R=64 equator, saddle c=1, bump h=0.5, bump h=0.05); N = 64 (hyperbolic k=1) | midpoint: N = 4 (sphere R=1, sphere R=10, sphere R=100, sphere R=1e4, sphere R=1e7, sphere R=1e8, torus R=2, torus R=64 equator, saddle c=1, bump h=0.5, bump h=0.05); N = 8 (hyperbolic k=1) | rk4: N = 4 (sphere R=1, sphere R=10, sphere R=100, sphere R=1e4, sphere R=1e7, sphere R=1e8, torus R=2, torus R=64 equator, saddle c=1, bump h=0.5, bump h=0.05, hyperbolic k=1); with rounding included, rounding changes the outcome for 5 (surface, method) pairs, all with |K| <= 1e-14. Optional SciPy DOP853 cross-check of the adaptive references: max |DOP853 - DP45 reference| = 3.4e-13 (artifact only; it shares ciw's right-hand side, so it checks the integrator, not the geometry).
observation_model: Computed deviation j_head,h(L) - L (an exact floating-point subtraction) against the true deviation, split into the method's truncation part and the run's rounding part; no renormalization.

title: Generate a report comparing intrinsic curvature effects with integrator error.
uncertainty: Reference spread up to 3.2e-12. Rounding parts are exact for constant K and estimated by a rescaled rerun for variable K; a rounding part above 0.1 of the truncation part (marked (r) in resolvability.md) occurs in 8 euler, 11 midpoint, 21 rk4 of 72 entries per method. Those ratios depend on the rounding sequence; they are kept in the artifacts and out of every checked ratio and witness except the K = 1e-16 floor finding, whose claim is about roundoff and whose computed deviations are exactly zero. The threshold 10 and the rounding share 0.1 are declared conventions.
unresolved_assumptions: Only j_head(L) is compared; the lateral column and conjugate-point locations are not
Variable-curvature paths add geodesic-position error to K(gamma(s)); its K-scaling is not separated here, and their rounding part is an estimate, not an exact split
The SciPy cross-check shares ciw's right-hand side and is independent in the integrator only
Measurement noise of any real observation is absent; sensor-level resolvability is not established
